Source: own Balance Sheet (Solo) 'As at 31 December 2024' lines ~11712-11800; own Profit & Loss Account (Solo) 'For the year ended 31 December 2024' lines ~11836-11900; Note 16.5 'Capital Adequacy (Solo Basis)' lines ~15093-15140; Note 7.8 'Particulars of provision for Investments' lines ~14150-14225; Annexure 'Financial Highlights (Solo)' lines ~16985-17010; Independent Auditor's Report (Qualified Opinion / Basis for Qualified Opinion / Material Uncertainty) lines ~10730-10800; '5 Years Key Financial Data' table lines ~6640-6680; Directors' Report Capital Base comparative table lines ~3790-3850. CRITICAL FY2024 FINDING: Auditors (Kazi Zahir Khan & Co. and Khan Wahab Shafique Rahman & Co.) issued a QUALIFIED OPINION with a 'Material Uncertainty' paragraph. Per Bangladesh Bank letter no. DBI-7/4(2)/2025-346 dated 29 April 2025, the Bank was required to maintain provisions of Taka 23,158.06 crore but maintained only Taka 1,502.62 crore plus paid Taka 78.18 crore; Bangladesh Bank letter no. DOS(CAMS)1157/41(Dividend)/2025-3109 dated 21 May 2025 permitted finalizing the FY2024 financial statements without provisioning the remainder (regulatory forbearance). The Material Uncertainty paragraph states reported CRAR of 6.43% would deteriorate to NEGATIVE 33.95% after considering the deferred provision shortfall, implying a total capital shortfall of Taka 22,850.14 crore against the 12.50% requirement. AT LEAST FOUR OTHER shortfall figures appear elsewhere in the SAME audited report, none reconciled to each other or to the two figures above: Note 7.8 and Note 16.5's footnote both give 'Provision Surplus/(Shortfall)' of exactly Taka (209,937,209,364) = 20,993.72 crore (this is the figure used for this dataset's implied shortfall, being the one corroborated identically in two separate notes plus the Financial Highlights annexure); Note 14.11's footnote gives a shortfall of Taka 21,626.58 crore per the same DBI letter, further reduced to a 'permitted' shortfall of Taka 21,577.26 crore per the same DOS letter (after requiring an incremental Taka 120 crore specific provision), against a stated total provision maintained of Taka 1,580.80 crore; the Directors' Report separately states a deferred provision shortfall of Taka 2,16,554.40 million = 21,655.44 crore. Per this dataset's convention, all figures are recorded verbatim rather than silently reconciled. Other Auditor findings: sponsor/director shareholding fell to 11.62% (below the BSEC-required 30% minimum); the Bank could not maintain CRR/SLR on multiple occasions during the year, resorting to Taka 9,084.75 crore of special liquidity support (Bangladesh Govt. Special Islamic Bond, IBLF, Bangladesh Bank overdraft, foreign-currency borrowing); customer (client) deposits fell 16.64% (Taka 345,955.93m to Taka 288,401.50m); Investment-Deposit Ratio reached 121.15% against a 92.5% regulatory cap; RWA nearly DOUBLED year-on-year (Taka 305,922.96m to Taka 519,943.53m) even as the balance sheet grew only modestly (Total Assets +0.07%), consistent with credit-risk-weight escalation from the asset-quality collapse (classified-investment ratio 4.79% to 61.74%) rather than balance-sheet growth. The bank swung from a pre-tax profit of Taka 3,963.89m (FY2023) to a pre-tax LOSS of Taka -319.51m (FY2024), and post-tax from +Taka 2,564.13m to -Taka 532.74m -- the first reported net loss in this dataset's SIBL series. DSE's own disclosure table separately shows a CONSOLIDATED FY2024 loss of Taka -1,017.03m (EPS -0.89), larger than the Solo loss recorded here, implying the two subsidiaries (SIBL Securities Ltd., SIBL Investment Ltd.) were also loss-making or consolidation adjustments amplified the loss; not independently verified in this dataset (Solo basis throughout, per project convention).

Income-statement items are CUMULATIVE from 1 January 2025 (Jan-1 through the end of this quarter), not discrete-quarter figures, per this project's convention (flagged via the _cumulative suffix, matching bank_financials/CITYBANK/quarterly/2024_Q1.json). Shariah-based Islamic bank: 'Investments' is the Shariah-compliant equivalent of conventional Loans and Advances; 'Profit paid on Deposits' is the equivalent of Interest Expense; 'Net Investment Income' is the equivalent of Net Interest Income -- consistent with the convention already used for this bank's Q4/annual series. Classified-investment (asset-quality/NPL) and Capital Adequacy (CRAR/Tier-1/Tier-2) figures are NOT disclosed in SIBL's interim quarterly/half-yearly filings at all (confirmed absent from every quarter's notes checked in this pass) -- this is a genuine limitation of the source documents themselves, not an extraction gap, so no classified_investments/npl_pct/car_pct/tier1/tier2/RWA fields are populated for any Q1-Q3 period in this dataset.

POST-GENERATION CORRECTION NOTE: several income-statement sub-line-items in this quarter's source page had systematic extraction defects (font/character corruption, dropped leading digits, or a wrong-column/wrong-row value) that were not caught by the balance-sheet-identity check alone. These were found and corrected using a second-pass internal-consistency audit (checking that Net Investment Income + Income from Shares + Commission + Other Operating Income sums to Total Operating Income, and that Total Operating Income minus Expenses minus Provision minus Tax chains correctly to Net Profit After Tax) before this file was finalized; corrected/added fields carry their own metric_note explaining the specific fix. Values that could not be reconstructed with confidence were omitted rather than guessed.

ratios.notes: 'gross_loans' field holds total Shariah-compliant Investment (General) -- the Islamic-banking equivalent of loans; 'npl_ratio_pct' holds the Ratio of Classified Investments to Total Investments. Equity was positive in every year 2010-2024 (including the FY2024 loss year), so the dataset's negative-equity-breaks-ROE rule was not triggered for SIBL; roa_pct/roe_pct are populated for all 15 years. UPDATED 2026-08-27: appended 37 Q1/Q2/Q3 interim periods (FY2012 H1 through FY2025 Q3) alongside the existing 15 Q4/annual periods above -- interim periods are distinguished by their 'quarter' field (Q1/Q2/Q3 vs Q4) and each carries its own 'period_type_note' explaining that npl_ratio_pct/car_pct are null (not disclosed in interim filings) and that eps/roa_pct/roe_pct inputs are cumulative-from-Jan-1. roa_pct/roe_pct for interim periods are annualized (x4 for Q1, x2 for Q2, x4/3 for Q3) using average of the prior FY's Q4 total_assets/equity and the current quarter's own total_assets/equity, per this dataset's stated ROA/ROE annualization convention (see _methodology.md); ldr_pct is calculated by this dataset (Investments / Deposits) since SIBL's own interim filings never state this ratio themselves (only its annual report does). Five quarters could not be sourced at all and have no entry here: 2012 Q1 (never published -- SIBL's own site's quarterly archive begins at H1 2012), 2012 Q3 and 2013 Q2 (the PDF at SIBL's own published URL for these periods was, on inspection, a different bank's report -- see sources.json), 2013 Q3 (the bank's own PDF's text layer was pervasively corrupted beyond safe extraction) and 2020 Q1 (PDF had no extractable text layer and was lost to a scratch-directory collision before OCR could be attempted -- see sources.json).

risk_signals.statement: The Ratio of Classified Investments to Total Investments (SIBL's Shariah-banking equivalent of the NPL ratio) exploded from 4.79% (FY2023) to 61.74% (FY2024) -- almost 13x in a single year, and one of the most severe single-year asset-quality deteriorations recorded anywhere in this dataset (comparable in scale to FIRSTSBANK's FY2024 jump to 91.75% and GIB's to 90.72%, both banks now merged with SIBL into Sammilito Islami Bank PLC). In absolute terms, classified investments rose from Taka 17,288.60m to Taka 236,579.50m against gross Investments (General) of Taka 383,165.07m.

Capital to Risk-weighted Asset Ratio (CRAR) fell from 12.66% (FY2023) to 6.43% (FY2024), breaching the 12.50% regulatory minimum (10% base plus 2.5% conservation buffer) by more than half. The bank's own auditors go further: the Independent Auditor's Report's Material Uncertainty paragraph states that if the deferred provision shortfall (see provision_shortfall_regulatory_forbearance_2024 below) were recognized, CRAR would deteriorate to NEGATIVE 33.95%, implying a total capital shortfall of Taka 22,850.14 crore against the requirement -- i.e. the reported 6.43% substantially overstates the bank's true capital position even before considering that Risk-Weighted Assets themselves nearly doubled the same year (Taka 305,922.96m to Taka 519,943.53m, +70.0%) while Total Assets grew only 0.07%, consistent with credit-risk-weight escalation driven by the asset-quality collapse rather than balance-sheet growth.

Per Bangladesh Bank letter no. DBI-7/4(2)/2025-346 (29 April 2025), cited in the Auditors' Basis for Qualified Opinion, SIBL was required to maintain provisions of Taka 23,158.06 crore but had maintained only Taka 1,502.62 crore (plus Taka 78.18 crore paid and included in profit paid on borrowings). Bangladesh Bank letter no. DOS(CAMS)1157/41(Dividend)/2025-3109 (21 May 2025) permitted the Bank to finalize its FY2024 financial statements without provisioning the remainder -- the same recognition-vs-deferral pattern this dataset's methodology documents for ISLAMIBANK, GIB and FIRSTSBANK. At least four further shortfall figures appear elsewhere in the SAME audited report without reconciliation to each other or to the figures above: Taka 20,993.72 crore (Note 7.8 and Note 16.5's footnote, identically, against a directly-reported classified-investment provision base); Taka 21,626.58 crore and a 'permitted' Taka 21,577.26 crore (Note 14.11's footnote, citing the same two Bangladesh Bank letters); and Taka 21,655.44 crore (the Directors' Report). This dataset records every figure verbatim per its never-silently-reconcile convention -- see the FY2024 quarterly JSON's period_note for the full citation trail.

SIBL swung from a pre-tax profit of Taka 3,963.89m (FY2023) to a pre-tax LOSS of Taka -319.51m (FY2024), and from a post-tax profit of Taka 2,564.13m to a post-tax LOSS of Taka -532.74m -- the first reported net loss anywhere in this dataset's SIBL series (FY2010-FY2024). Return on Equity fell from 11.89% to -2.48% and Return on Assets from 0.56% to -0.11%. Equity itself remained positive throughout (Taka 20,613.45m at FY2024 year-end, down from Taka 22,383.44m), so this dataset's negative-equity-breaks-ROE rule was not triggered; the -2.48% ROE is a straightforward (and already severe) calculation. DSE's own disclosure table separately shows a larger Consolidated-basis FY2024 loss of Taka -1,017.03m (EPS -0.89) versus this dataset's Solo-basis Taka -532.74m (EPS -0.88), implying SIBL's two wholly-owned subsidiaries (SIBL Securities Limited, SIBL Investment Limited) were also loss-making in FY2024 or that consolidation adjustments amplified the loss -- not independently verified in this Solo-basis dataset.

Client (customer) deposits fell 16.64% in FY2024, from Taka 345,955.93m to Taka 288,401.50m, per the Auditors' own Material Uncertainty paragraph -- confirmed exactly from this dataset's own stored figures ((345955.93-288401.50)/345955.93 = 16.64%). Total deposits (including interbank/placement-sourced deposits) fell a smaller 13.32% (Taka 357,388.85m to Taka 309,770.55m), while Placement from Other Banks & Financial Institutions more than doubled (Taka 43,280.00m to Taka 90,847.46m per the Balance Sheet), consistent with the Auditors' separate observation of 'increased placement liabilities of Taka 9,085 crore' -- i.e. the bank substantially replaced fleeing customer deposits with more expensive interbank/wholesale funding and Bangladesh Bank liquidity support (see going_concern_liquidity_support_2024 below). The Investment-Deposit (ID) Ratio consequently spiked to 121.15%, breaching Bangladesh Bank's 92.5% regulatory cap by nearly 29 percentage points.

The Auditors' Emphasis of Matter paragraph (b) discloses that SIBL could not maintain its Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) and Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) on multiple occasions during FY2024, and only reported positive CRR/SLR at year-end by drawing Taka 9,084.75 crore of special liquidity support (Bangladesh Government Special Islamic Bond, Islami Bank Liquidity Facility, direct Bangladesh Bank liquidity support, Bangladesh Bank overdraft, and foreign-currency borrowing from other banks) -- a scale of central-bank-dependent liquidity support equal to roughly 4.4x the bank's own FY2024 Total Shareholders' Equity (Taka 20,613.45m) -- i.e. the emergency liquidity support alone was more than four times the bank's entire remaining capital base. The Auditors also separately noted 5.85% of FY2024 investment income (Taka 185.29 crore of Taka 3,169.67 crore total) was charged on irregular-investment clients identified by Bangladesh Bank in April 2024, who remained non-performing as of the report date. The Bank's opinion was not modified for these matters, but they were disclosed as Emphasis of Matter alongside the Material Uncertainty paragraph on capital adequacy.

SIBL never published a standalone FY2025 annual report. It was declared a failed/non-viable institution and placed under resolution, then merged by Bangladesh Bank into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, together with four other crisis-hit Shariah banks already confirmed in this dataset to have no FY2025 report for the identical reason (EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Union Bank). DSE's disclosure table shows SIBL continued filing unaudited quarterly results through Q3 2025 (9-month cumulative EPS -15.28, itself indicating continued severe losses through September 2025 -- roughly 17x FY2024's full-year per-share loss of -0.88 already registered in just three quarters) but its 'Annual' column for FY2025 was never populated, and its market price fell from Tk 10.1 to Tk 4.4 per share over the same three quarters. SIBL's own website (siblbd.com) has itself been rebranded to 'Sammilito Islami Bank PLC' as of this dataset's retrieval date (26 August 2026). This is a confirmed, permanent series-end for SIBL as a standalone reporting entity.

Prior to FY2024, SIBL's FY2010-FY2023 series shows sustained balance-sheet growth (Total Assets Taka 55,168.54m to Taka 476,051.86m, roughly 8.6x over 13 years) with generally stable capital adequacy (CRAR ranged 9.33%-14.27%, never breaching the regulatory minimum in any year shown) and healthy profitability (ROE ranged 8.78%-16.89%; ROA ranged 0.42%-2.39%). Asset quality fluctuated but stayed within a 3.33%-8.20% classified-investment-ratio band throughout FY2010-FY2022, ticking down again to 4.79% in FY2023 -- giving no indication in this dataset's own numbers, as late as the FY2023 year-end, of the scale of the FY2024 collapse that followed. This is consistent with the pattern this dataset's methodology has already observed at other Shariah banks now also part of the Sammilito Islami Bank merger (EXIMBANK, FIRSTSBANK, GIB): a long period of unremarkable, even healthy-looking reported metrics, followed by a single catastrophic recognition year once regulatory/political pressure (the post-2024 scrutiny of S-Alam-Group-linked and other distressed Islamic banks) forced disclosure.

Q1-Q3 2024/2025 interim filings (added 2026-08-27; the FY2024/FY2025 signals above were derived from annual/DSE data alone) show the crisis was visible in real time, well before either the FY2024 annual report (published mid-2025) or the risk signals above could reflect it. (1) LDR/Investment-Deposit ratio: this dataset's own calculation (SIBL's interim filings do not state the ratio themselves) already showed 108.90% at Q1 2024 (reviewed by the Audit Committee 05 May 2024, per that filing's own Note 2.6) -- above the 92.5% regulatory cap from the very first quarter of the crisis year, ten months before the FY2024 year-end figure of 121.15% was disclosed. It continued 104.95% (Q2) and 115.33% (Q3) through the rest of 2024, never returning below the cap. (2) Pre-provision operating profit (SIBL's own 'Profit/(Loss) before Provision' line) swung to a discrete-quarter LOSS of Taka -500.31m in Q3 2024 alone (Jul-Sep) -- Q3 2024's cumulative Jan-Sept figure of Taka 1,185.77m was actually LOWER than Q2 2024's cumulative Jan-June figure of Taka 1,686.08m, meaning the quarter itself was loss-making before any provisioning was even applied, a full quarter before the FY2024 audited loss (Taka -532.74m PAT) was reported. (3) The crisis did not end with FY2024: 2025's interim filings show continuous, worsening losses -- Q1 2025 PAT -1,482.82m (annualized ROA -1.25%, ROE -29.94%), Q2 2025 cumulative PAT -4,692.16m (annualized ROA -2.00%, ROE -51.72%), Q3 2025 cumulative PAT -17,036.84m (annualized ROA -4.85%, ROE -190.76%). Isolating Q3 2025 alone (cumulative minus H1): a discrete-quarter net loss of Taka -12,344.68m and a discrete-quarter pre-provision operating loss of Taka -8,322.93m -- the single worst quarter in this dataset's SIBL series, roughly 23.2x the size of the entire FY2024 full-year loss (Taka -532.74m) that had already triggered the qualified audit opinion, Material Uncertainty paragraph and eventual Sammilito Islami Bank merger. Total Shareholders' Equity (Solo), which stood at Taka 20,613.45m at FY2024 year-end, had fallen to just Taka 3,203.02m by Q3 2025 (30 September 2025) -- an 84.5% erosion in three quarters -- confirming the FY2024 qualified opinion was the beginning of the collapse, not its resolution. Cross-validated against DSE's own 'Interim Financial Performance: 2025' disclosure table (Basic EPS: Q1 -1.410, H1 cumulative -4.330, 9-month cumulative -15.280, with Q3 alone at -10.940 -- by far the single worst quarter shown), which independently confirms the same dramatic Q3 2025 deterioration on a per-share basis.

insights.historical_context: Social Islami Bank (SIBL, later Social Islami Bank PLC) presents, across FY2010-FY2024, one of the clearest 'stable-for-a-decade-plus-then-sudden-collapse' patterns in this dataset. From FY2010 to FY2023 the bank grew its balance sheet roughly 8.6x (Total Assets Taka 55,168.54m to Taka 476,051.86m) while keeping CRAR consistently above the regulatory minimum (range 9.33%-14.27%) and ROE in a healthy 8.78%-16.89% range, with a classified-investment ratio that never exceeded 8.20% in any of those fourteen years. FY2024 changed everything: the classified-investment ratio rocketed to 61.74%, CRAR fell to 6.43% (or an auditor-estimated -33.95% once a Taka 20,993.72-23,158.06 crore provision shortfall -- reported inconsistently across at least five places in the same audited report -- is fully recognized), and the bank posted its first-ever net loss in this dataset's series (Solo PAT -532.74m; Consolidated -1,017.03m per DSE). Client deposits fled (-16.64%), replaced by more than doubled interbank placement liabilities and by roughly Tk 9,085 crore of Bangladesh-Bank-brokered liquidity support just to maintain positive CRR/SLR at year-end. As with EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank and Global Islami Bank -- all already documented in this dataset -- SIBL's FY2024 shock proved to be a terminal event rather than a recoverable downturn: it was declared a failed institution, placed under Bangladesh Bank resolution, and merged into a new state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, together with those same three banks plus Union Bank. No standalone FY2025 report exists or will exist; SIBL's own former website now identifies itself as Sammilito Islami Bank PLC. Ranking SIBL purely on FY2023 reported profitability (Taka 2,564.13m, ROE 11.89%) would have placed it among this dataset's healthier mid-sized banks one year before its collapse -- a caution this dataset's methodology has repeatedly found holds across the Shariah-banking segment (see also ISLAMIBANK's unprovisioned-NPL pattern in _cross_bank.json), and a reminder that a single audited year's reported profit is a poor predictor of the next year's solvency for this cohort of banks.

sources.notes: No FY2025 (year ended 31 December 2025) annual report or standalone audited financial statements exist for Social Islami Bank as an independent entity, confirmed via a time-boxed check across three independent channels (approx. 15-20 minutes of research, consistent with this dataset's precedent for the other four banks in the same merger): (1) DSE's own dynamically-updated company page (dsebd.org/displayCompany.php?name=SIBL, fetched via curl due to a WebFetch TLS-certificate error on the domain) shows the 'Financial Performance as per Audited Financial Statements' table stopping at FY2024 (EPS -0.89 consolidated, NAV/share 18.15, Profit for the year -1,017.03m -- all consistent with this dataset's independently-sourced FY2024 Solo figures), and its 'Interim Financial Performance: 2025' table shows populated quarterly EPS through Q3 2025 (Q1 -1.410, Half-Yearly cumulative -4.330, 9-Months cumulative -15.280, market price collapsing from Tk 10.1 to Tk 4.4 over the year) with the 'Annual' column explicitly blank ('-') for every row -- the same 'quarterly data continues, annual column stays blank' signature already documented for EXIMBANK and GIB; (2) a Wayback Machine CDX search of siblbd.com's report-hosting paths (annual_report/*, assets/reports/annual/*, assets/reports/annual_statements/*; ~110 report-related URLs found across all naming conventions used over the site's history) finds 'SIBL_Annual_Report_2024.pdf' and 'Annual_Financial_Statements_2024.pdf' as the latest crawled annual filings under every tested naming convention, with no 2025-year file of any kind; (3) SIBL's own live homepage (siblbd.com, fetched 2026-08-26) has itself been rebranded and now identifies the institution as 'Sammilito Islami Bank PLC', referencing an 11th Board of Directors meeting of 'Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, a state-owned Shariah-based bank' dated 25 August 2026 (the day before this retrieval) -- the single strongest piece of evidence found across this dataset's five merged-bank investigations, since it is the bank's own current self-identification rather than a third-party report. REASON: per WebSearch results (The Daily Star, BSS News, Wikipedia's 'Sammilito Islami Bank' article), Social Islami Bank PLC was declared a failed/non-viable institution and placed under resolution under the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025, then merged into a newly formed state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, together with four other crisis-hit Shariah banks already confirmed in this dataset to have no FY2025 report for the identical reason (EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Union Bank). Bangladesh Bank issued a Letter of Intent and no-objection certificate for Sammilito Islami Bank on 9 November 2025 (before FY2025/Dec-2025 had even closed); press coverage variously describes Sammilito Islami Bank beginning operations in early December 2025 and, per the concurrently-researched GIB/EXIMBANK sessions in this dataset, 18 August 2026 as a date associated with the transition to fully independent (non-administrator-led) operations -- the exact operational-handover date differs slightly across sources and was not further reconciled, as it does not change the conclusion. CONCLUSION: this is a confirmed, permanent series-end for SIBL as an independently reporting entity, not an ordinary reporting lag. Total time spent on this FY2025 investigation: approximately 20 minutes (one WebSearch, two WebFetch calls, one DSE curl fetch, one Wayback CDX pass), consistent with the task's time-boxing instruction given the strong prior expectation from the other four merged banks already in this dataset.
